name: Core
description: Core node catalog — infrastructure + storage + windows + scripts + api routes

actions.label: Set SSH Key
actions.description: Assign a Key Store key to this server (key reference is "<keyStoreNodeId>:<keyName>"). With install=true, also append the key's public half to the remote's authorized_keys using the server's current credentials.

install.description: Also install the public key on the remote's authorized_keys (default: false)

actions.label: Accept Host Key
actions.description: Scan the remote host key and pin it into known_hosts so OpenSSH-based transports (e.g. docker over ssh://) stop failing host-key verification.

actions.label: Generate Key
actions.description: Generate a new SSH keypair in this Key Store. Returns the key name and type — never private key material.

actions.label: List Keys
actions.description: List keys in this store with their type and fingerprint. Does not expose private key material.

actions.label: Delete Key
actions.description: Delete a key (and its public key) from this store.

name.description: Name of the key to delete

actions.label: Generate Secret
actions.description: Create or rotate a secret with a server-side random value. Absent name creates it, existing name rotates it. Returns the name and created/rotated status — never the value.

name.description: Secret name to create or rotate

actions.description: Execute the script in the connected terminal context (or local if none).

actions.label: Send
actions.description: Deliver a message to an agent through this node — same routing as a wired text-in delivery (session reuse/create, envelope composition, hidden-by-default registration). agent/job fall back to this node's configured defaults when omitted. Pass `thread` instead to deliver into a group-chat thread this node's own wiring can reach — mutually exclusive with agent/job/key/session. Returns, for an agent:job send, the target session key, whether a new session was created and whether force actually interrupted a running turn; for a thread send, the thread reference and whether it queued behind a running turn or was delivered immediately. Never the message content.

agent.description: Target agent slug; falls back to this node's default agent

job.description: Target job slug; falls back to this node's default job

key.description: Optional session discriminator — same agent+job with a different key is a distinct, stable session

title.description: Optional session title, applied only when the session is first created

session.description: Legacy combined "agent:<agent>:<job>" key, honored when agent/job are omitted

force.description: Cancel the agent's in-flight turn (if any) and enqueue this message after whatever's already queued, instead of waiting behind it. This interrupts the agent mid-work — use for urgent/corrective messages, not routine sends. No effect if the session isn't currently running a turn.

thread.description: A group-chat thread reference ("<group-slug>:<agent-slug>:<thread-slug>", a whole session key, or a thread id) to deliver into, instead of an agent:job session. Mutually exclusive with agent/job/key/session — carrying both is refused. Delivered only when the thread's own agent is one this node's wiring could otherwise reach; refused, clearly, for an unknown or unreachable thread.

actions.label: List Agents
actions.description: Enumerate the agents (and their jobs) this node can route to via `send` — same space, same slug resolution, so any value returned here is guaranteed to route.

actions.label: List Sessions
actions.description: List the sessions this node can reach (same agent/job resolution as `send`) — compact navigation info only, never message content. Each session's `status` is the same offline/idle/working/waiting vocabulary the chat list uses: waiting = blocked on a permission request, working = a turn is running, idle = process alive but neither, offline = no process. Each also carries `contextUsage`: `{ usedTokens, contextLimit, asOf? }` as last reported by that session's own harness, never estimated here. An `offline` session with prior activity reports its last-known reading here too, with `asOf` (ms since epoch) set — its absence means the figure is live. `contextUsage` is null only when it is genuinely UNKNOWN — never loaded, not finished a turn since it was loaded, or a harness that does not report usage — and null must not be read as "nothing held"; `contextLimit` alone is null when the harness cannot say what the model's window is, so a ratio cannot always be computed. Use it to spot a session that should be compacted before it fills (see the `compact` action). Optionally filter by agent and/or job slug.

agent.description: Only sessions for this agent slug

job.description: Only sessions for this job slug

actions.label: List Turns
actions.description: Tail-first, cursor-paged view of a session's turns (a sessionKey from listSessions) — truncated prompt/final-message text only, never the full event stream. Omit beforeIndex for the most recent turns; pass a previous page's nextBeforeIndex to page further back. Response includes `sessionStatus` (same vocabulary as listSessions): `offline` means the session has no live process, so an empty `turns` array there means "nothing to load", not "empty session". A turn's own `status` is `unknown` when it was restored by a session/load replay after a restart — it ended, but the replay does not record how, so treat it as neither success nor failure.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions

turns.description: Number of turns to return (default 10, capped at 50)

beforeIndex.description: Cursor from a previous page's nextBeforeIndex — fetches the turns immediately before it

actions.label: Compact Session
actions.description: Request compaction of a session's context and return immediately — this call never blocks for the compaction itself; poll `compactStatus` with the same sessionKey for the outcome. An `offline` session is woken from its stored state first (the same resume a message sent to it would trigger) and left running afterwards — compaction never leaves a session offline, since re-orienting from the re-delivered task context and standing instructions is the point. Errors synchronously only when the session cannot be resumed at all (nothing was ever persisted for this key). A `working` or `waiting` session is NOT an error here — the request queues behind whatever turn is currently running and executes once the session goes idle, without ever interrupting that turn (same no-interrupt principle as an ordinary queued message). A second `compact` call for a session that already has a pending or running compaction COALESCES into it instead of starting a duplicate — `coalesced: true` in the response tells a caller that re-fires (e.g. after not waiting for a previous ack) that it did not start a second compaction. Once it actually runs: `/compact`, then a re-send of that session's task context and standing instructions, because compaction summarises the conversation and drops the original messages — including the ones that carried them. See `compactStatus`'s description for what the eventual result contains. WHEN to compact is the caller's policy, not this action's.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions

actions.label: Compact Status
actions.description: The queryable signal that a `compact` request actually ran — the only way to observe its outcome, since `compact` itself returns before the compaction happens. `state` is `never-requested` (no compact has ever been requested for this sessionKey since the server last started), `pending` (queued, waiting for the session's current turn to end), `running` (the /compact turn or the instruction restore is in flight now), `done`, or `error` (the compaction job itself failed unexpectedly — distinct from `result.compacted: false`, which is a completed job that determined nothing shrank). `result` is present once `state` is `done`: `contextUsageBefore`/`contextUsageAfter` (same shape and same null-means-unknown rule as listSessions) BRACKET THE `/compact` TURN ALONE — the after-reading is taken before any instructions are re-sent, so it reports what compaction freed and is not reduced by the cost of restoring them. `compacted` is true when the held context shrank, false when it GREW (a harness with no `/compact` answers it as an ordinary message, so it ends up holding more — this is the failure signal, not a clean delivery), and null when it cannot be told: usage unknown on either side, or an unchanged figure, which is indistinguishable from a reading that has not refreshed. `instructionsRestored` reports whether the re-sent instructions were actually read (not merely sent) — it is false when `compacted` is false, since nothing was dropped and re-sending would only grow the context this action exists to shrink, and also false when the session had no task context or instructions to restore. A job's status is retained only until superseded by a new `compact` request for the same sessionKey; there is no history beyond the most recent one.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions

actions.label: Unload Session
actions.description: Terminate an idle session's process to free the RAM it holds while it isn't doing anything. The session's transcript and its durable session pointer are left untouched — the next message sent to this sessionKey reloads it transparently (the same cold-start resume an `offline` session already uses), so nothing about the conversation is lost. Only applies to a session whose `status` (see `listSessions`) is `idle`: `offline` has no process to unload and errors synchronously, and `working`/`waiting` also error rather than unload, since that session's own harness may own background work a kill would silently drop with no way to resume it.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions

actions.label: Delete Session
actions.description: Remove a session for good: drops its durable session pointer (so it can never cold-start resume, unlike `unload`) and its chat-list entry (so it also stops appearing in the sidebar). By default this only works on a session whose `status` (see `listSessions`) is `offline` — the normal case, e.g. clearing out stale sessions nobody is using — and errors synchronously for `idle`/`working`/`waiting`, since deleting a live session also ends its process and would silently drop whatever it's doing. Pass `force: true` to override: it ends the live process first (same teardown a live chat delete already uses) and then deletes. Unlike deleting a chat in the UI, this does not touch the underlying harness's on-disk transcript — that stays intentionally out of reach, the same harness-agnostic boundary session loading already observes (the harness may even be running on a different terminal context — local/WSL/SSH — than this server), so the transcript file is orphaned on disk, not deleted, and not tracked by anything afterward.

sessionKey.description: Session key, as returned by listSessions

force.description: Delete even if the session is idle/working/waiting, ending its live process first. Without this, a non-offline session is refused rather than silently interrupted.

contexts.label: Terminal Context
contexts.description: Terminal execution context (local, WSL, or SSH)

contexts.label: Execution Context
contexts.description: Async execution context for request/response handlers
